transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (CTO, NovaChat), Ethan Morales (ML Eng), Sara Lee (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick migration demo and parity mapping for NovaChat's stack which currently uses OpenAI for chat completions, Anthropic for safety checks, and Together for fine-tuned models. Show Redwood API equivalents (chat, embeddings, streaming, function/tool calling), discuss Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private for data residency and latency, and propose a 2-week POC with benchmarks.

Topics:
- API parity: parameters, streaming, function calling
- Embeddings parity and dimensions
- Model routing and fallbacks (latency/cost)
- Dedicated/Private deployment options, VPC/KMS, SOC2
- Benchmark plan and success criteria

Action items (mentioned above)

Transcript body:
00:00 Lena Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro, I'm lena from Redwood, ae on this account, with marcus our se from the inference team, over to priya to do a quick context of your current stack
00:18 Priya Singh: yeah thanks lena, um so quick overview, we run our chat product on OpenAI chat completions - mostly gpt-4-ish family but we also have a handful of Anthropic calls for safety scoring, and Together for some tuned models. main concerns are latency for real-time chat, cost, and data residency for EU customers.
00:40 Marcus Chen: cool thanks priya, and ethan, sara, feel free to chime in. quick q, what's your current p95 on latency for chat?
00:48 Ethan Morales: p95 is about 380 ms for short prompts, but spikes during peak are up to ~800ms cause of batching and retries.
00:56 Sara Lee: and we need SOC2 level logs and KMS integration, plus a VPC option for EU region.
01:05 Lena Park: totally, that's in line with what we help with. demo plan: we'll show parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API, walk through console for routing and observability, and then talk deployment options for Dedicated/Private. any adjustments?
01:20 Priya Singh: sounds good. also curious about fine-tuning or quantized model support — Together is giving us cost wins there.
01:28 Marcus Chen: good call. Redwood supports quantized variants and model recommendations in Optimize that help with CPU/GPU tradeoffs; we'll demo the model catalog and quant suggestions briefly.
01:36 -- 02:00 (brief audio glitch, background typing) --
02:05 Marcus Chen: jumping into the parity: the Redwood "chat" endpoint maps to OpenAI chat completions pretty directly. fields: model -> model, messages -> messages, temperature/top_p behave the same, and we expose streaming with chunked tokens and delta events for UI. the differences: we add routing headers for tenant and fallback preferences, and our SDK includes a compact wrapper for function/tool calling to match both anthro and openai function calls.
02:40 Ethan Morales: when you say function/tool calling, is that one-to-one with OpenAI's function spec? we use that a lot for structured actions.
02:48 Marcus Chen: yes, we support the same shape for function definitions and structured responses, though the event format in streaming has slight naming diffs, and we provide a small migration helper script that converts OpenAI's json schema to Redwood's expected envelope. we'll share the snippet.
03:10 Lena Park: for embeddings, we map OpenAI embeddings endpoint to Redwood embeddings; dimension differences exist by model but we surfaced a mapping table — e.g., text-embedding-ada-002 -> redwood-embed-small (1536 dims), and for anthro embeddings we'd map to redwood-embed-legacy or custom tuned vectors.
03:35 Priya Singh: important for us is semantic search parity, vector store compat. can you confirm vector outputs are float32 and same normalization?
03:42 Marcus Chen: yes outputs are float32 by default and we include options for l2 or cosine prep normalization. small variance can appear with quantized or 8-bit models, we'll flag those in the parity matrix.
03:55 -- 04:30 (crosstalk, someone off mic) --
04:35 Marcus Chen: now about streaming and latency: Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and KV caching; for chat use cases with repeated context we can keep KV cache warm to cut token generation latency. your 380ms p95 should be reachable — we typically hit sub-200ms p95 on dedicated pools for short responses for similar workloads.
05:00 Ethan Morales: what's the tradeoff? are you doing more eager batching that could increase tail?
05:06 Marcus Chen: it's workload-aware; the serving runtime adapts. there are config levers in Console to prioritize latency over cost — e.g., reduce batch window, pin to dedicated capacity, and enable prefix caching. Optimize will also recommend batching settings per endpoint.
05:25 Priya Singh: about privacy, we need VPC/private deployment and KMS for key control. is Private fully air-gapped?
05:31 Lena Park: we offer Private with a customer-controlled control plane and optional on-prem package; KMS/HSM integrations are supported. for strict air-gapped installs we can coordinate with our infra team — expect longer lead times. we'll include onboarding checklist in the security pack.
05:45 Sara Lee: audit logs and RBAC? we need SSO/SAML and per-team RBAC.
05:50 Marcus Chen: yes SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC, and audit logs are standard enterprise features; logs can be routed to your SIEM and we retain per-request metadata for the configured retention window.
06:05 Priya Singh: on the topic of fallbacks — we sometimes route to a cheaper model on cost spikes. does Redwood support model routing and automated fallback?
06:12 Marcus Chen: yep, smart routing policies: route by latency, cost, region, and we can define fallback chains (e.g., model-a -> model-b -> synthetic response). Redwood can automatically downgrade to cached responses or shorter completions to preserve SLOs.
06:30 Lena Park: quick demo share — I'll pull up the Console to show model catalog and routing rules.
06:45 -- 07:20 (screen share opens, slight lag) --
07:22 Lena Park: on screen, model catalog, you can see curated profiles, perf numbers, and quantization options. this is where you'd pin a model for a route. note the recommended quant profile for chat-light to get cost down ~30% while keeping quality.
07:45 Ethan Morales: can we upload a tuned Together model? we have a few fine-tunes there.
07:52 Marcus Chen: we support model variants and bring-your-own-model in Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we can host vetted tuned models depending on licensing. for Dedicated, you can bring the artifact and we handle deployment. we'll add this to the POC plan.
08:10 Priya Singh: what about response parity — we've seen subtle output differences between providers affecting intent classification downstream. how do you validate that?
08:18 Marcus Chen: two parts: 1) the parity matrix with example prompts and outputs, and 2) our Quality monitoring in Optimize — you can upload eval sets, and we alert on regressions. we'll also run a small baseline during the POC to compare intent metrics.
08:35 -- 09:00 (typing, brief pause) --
09:05 Marcus Chen: diving into sample request mapping — here's an example cURL for OpenAI chat: curl openai.com/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"gpt-4", "messages": [...] }'--- Redwoods equivalent is curl api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H 'x-tenant: nova' -d '{"model":"redwood-gpt4-compat", "messages": [...], "stream": true}' we also provide middleware migration helpers for node/python.
09:45 Ethan Morales: will our existing SDK calls break? we use a forked openai js sdk with a wrapper.
09:51 Marcus Chen: minimal changes — mostly endpoint and minor event naming; we included an adapter snippet that maps the streaming events back to openai event names so client code can remain unchanged in many cases. will send snippet.
10:10 Priya Singh: latency of 200ms mentioned for dedicated — what if we go hosted?
10:16 Marcus Chen: hosted varies more; p95 for hosted is typically 250-400ms depending on region and model size. Dedicated provides the tightest tail guarantees, and Dedicated Reserved capacity helps with predictable throughput and lower unit cost.
10:30 Lena Park: here's a typical POC plan we propose: 2 weeks, baseline run with your representative prompts, measure latency/cost/quality, and then tweak batching/quant profiles. we run that with a small reserved pool for the pilot.
10:45 Sara Lee: for the POC we'll need IP allowlist and possibly a VPN peering for Private.
10:50 Lena Park: yes we can support IP allowlist and VPN peering, Marcus will collect the network diagram.
11:00 -- 11:30 (short pause while Marcus opens benchmark doc) --
11:32 Marcus Chen: benchmarks: we'll run a mix of 20% long-context prompts, 70% short chat, 10% embeddings; target 5k QPS/day across the test and we'll give cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated.
11:50 Priya Singh: about price — how does pricing compare to OpenAI per token?
11:55 Lena Park: varies by model and reserved commit. generally you can expect 0.6-0.9x on token cost with optimized quantization and Dedicated. for embeddings we often see better per-vector pricing with higher volume commitments. we'll include ranges in the proposal.
12:12 Ethan Morales: any gotchas with KV cache and context windows? we use long contexts ~8k tokens for some flows.
12:19 Marcus Chen: the runtime supports large context windows and selects kernels accordingly; for extremely long contexts we recommend dedicated pool with larger memory GPUs and enabling prefix KV caching. Optimize will flag token-cost hot spots.
12:35 Priya Singh: security pack — can you outline what you send?
12:41 Lena Park: SOC2 report, SOC2-plus artifacts for Dedicated/Private, SSO/SAML config guide, KMS/HSM integration notes, network/connectivity checklist, and data retention policy. we'll attach the docs.
12:55 Sara Lee: who will own the timeline if we sign up? we have internal procurement windows.
13:00 Lena Park: I'll be your primary owner for contracting, Marcus will run the technical POC and liaise with engineering during onboarding.
13:08 Priya Singh: ok great. one last question: Anthropic safety checks — can Redwood call out to an external safety model or integrate existing Anthropic calls during transition?
13:17 Marcus Chen: yes, you can chain calls — Redwood routing supports multi-model orchestration; during POC we can keep Anthropic for safety scoring while shifting chat to Redwood, so you can compare side-by-side.
13:31 -- 14:00 (wrap-up, summary) --
14:02 Lena Park: recap: send parity matrix + adapter snippets (Lena), Marcus runs benchmarks and provides sample runbook (Marcus), NovaChat to share network diagram and success criteria (Priya/Sara). propose start of POC next monday if that works.
14:25 Priya Singh: monday works, we'll confirm internal. thanks, that was helpful.
14:32 Ethan Morales: thanks everyone.
14:35 Lena Park: thanks all — we'll follow up with the security pack and the parity artifacts.
14:45 (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional naming errors and punctuation inconsistencies reflect typical Fireflies export. references to product names slightly varied (e.g., "redwood" vs "Redwood API", "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache").
